blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting enables efficient generalizable novel view synthesis, but existing pixel-aligned methods often generate highly redundant Gaussian primitives, causing the final representation size and rendering cost to grow rapidly with image resolution and the number of input views. We propose BudgetSplat, a budget-controllable feed-forward framework that adapts the final Gaussian representation to a user-specified preservation ratio. Rather than treating compaction as simple importance ranking, we formulate it as a joint problem of importance estimation, spatial coverage, and cross-view redundancy. A single trained model supports varying numbers of context views and multiple test-time budgets without per-budget retraining or per-scene compression. To realize this formulation, Intra-Cross Mask Supervision provides structure-, coverage-, and redundancy-aware guidance for learning Gaussian importance, while budget-conditioned feature modulation adapts Gaussian opacity and attributes to the requested preservation ratio. Coverage-Aware Budget Selection further combines patch-wise pre-selection, view-wise opacity ranking, and 3D redundancy suppression to construct compact yet spatially distributed Gaussian representations. Experiments on indoor reconstruction and cross-dataset generalization demonstrate consistent quality--size trade-offs across different input view counts and preservation ratios, substantially reducing final representation storage and rendering cost while preserving rendering quality.
blocks.zh: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splating可以实现高效的泛泛小说视图合成,但现有的像素对齐方法往往产生高度冗余的高斯原始,导致最终的表示大小和渲染成本随着图像分辨率和输入视图的数量而迅速增长. 我们提出预算PatricsSplat,一个预算可控的feed-forward框架,使最终的高斯代表制适应用户指定的保存比例. 我们不把紧凑作为简单的重要性排名,而是把它当作一个重要估计、空间覆盖和交叉视图冗余的共同问题。 单一的训练有素的模式支持不同数量的背景观点和多个测试时间预算,而无需按预算再培训或每场压缩. 为了实现这一配方,内十字面具监督公司为学习高斯文的重要性提供结构,覆盖范围,和冗余意识的指导,而预算有条件的特征调制则使高斯文不透明,属性适应所要求的保存比例. 覆盖-智能预算选择进一步结合了补丁预选,视图不透明排序,以及3D冗余压制,以构建紧凑但空间分布的高斯表示. 关于室内重建和跨数据集通用化的实验表明,不同输入视图计数和保存比率之间在质量大小上的取舍是一致的,大大减少了最后的表示储存量,在保持提供质量的同时降低了提供成本。

blocks.en: 1. Introduction
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 导言

blocks.en: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3D-GS) [ 9 ] represents scenes using explicit anisotropic Gaussians and enables high-quality real-time novel view synthesis. However, it requires costly per-scene optimization. Recent generalizable methods predict Gaussian representations from input images in a feed-forward manner, substantially improving reconstruction efficiency and generalization to unseen scenes [ 2 , 5 , 20 , 23 , 11 ] .
blocks.zh: 3D Gaussian Splateting (3D-GS) [9] 代表场景使用显式异同位素 Gaussians,并能够进行高质量的实时取景合成. 然而,这需要代价高昂的人均场景优化。 最近通用的方法预测了高斯人从输入图像中以反馈的方式呈现出来,大大提高了重建效率和泛化到看不见的场景[2,5,20,23,11].

blocks.en: Most feed-forward 3D-GS methods decode one or more Gaussians from each pixel. Although this pixel-aligned formulation provides strong geometric anchoring, its representation size grows rapidly with image resolution and input-view number. Overlapping observations additionally produce many redundant Gaussians, increasing the storage and rendering costs of the final scene asset. Existing methods reduce pixel-aligned Gaussian redundancy through different designs. Geometry-aware fusion [ 20 , 21 ] and view compression [ 18 ] consolidate overlapping pixel-aligned predictions across views; voxel-aligned prediction [ 19 ] predicts Gaussians in a shared 3D volume, whereas global scene encoders [ 1 , 8 ] compress multi-view observations into a compact set of scene tokens before decoding the Gaussian representation. The latter demonstrate that a fixed-capacity Gaussian set can be sufficient on some benchmarks, but its output size remains tied to the scene token capacity.
blocks.zh: 大多数Feed-forward 3D-GS方法从每个像素解码一个或多个高斯人. 虽然这种像素配对的配体提供了强烈的几何锚定,但其代表大小随着图像分辨率和输入视图数的迅速增长. 重叠观测还额外产生了许多冗余的高斯人,增加了最终场景资产的存储和渲染成本. 现有方法通过不同的设计来减少像素对齐的高斯冗余. 几何感知聚[20,21]和视图压缩[18]整合了各种观点的重叠像素对齐的预测;voxel对齐的预测[19]预测. Gaussians在共享的3D卷中,而全球场景编码器[1,8]在解码Gaussian代表符前将多视图观测压缩成一组紧凑的场景符号. 后者表明,在某些基准上,固定容量的高斯集可以足够,但其输出大小仍与场景标志容量挂钩.

blocks.en: These developments raise a practical question: Can a single feed-forward model adapt its final Gaussian representation to different user-specified budgets? Existing approaches generally fall into two categories. Fixed-capacity methods [ 1 , 8 ] tie the representation size to a particular token or decoder configuration, so substantially larger or more complex scenes may require retraining a higher-capacity model. Post-hoc compression methods [ 7 ] reduce an already reconstructed Gaussian set, but introduce additional per-scene processing or optimization. In practice, deployment conditions may require the same model to operate under different representation budgets. Simply applying a budget-unaware Top- K K rule to a conventionally trained pixel-aligned model is suboptimal: it may over-allocate Gaussians to salient or high-opacity regions, leaving weakly textured areas under-covered. We therefore view budget-controlled Gaussian compaction as a joint problem of importance estimation, spatial coverage, and cross-view redundancy, rather than simple candidate ranking. These limitations motivate a feed-forward model whose final Gaussian representation can be adjusted at test time while retaining the geometric advantages of pixel-aligned reconstruction.
blocks.zh: 这些事态发展提出了一个实际问题: 一个单一的Feed-forward模型能否根据不同的用户特定预算调整其最终的高斯代表? 现行办法一般分为两类。 固定容量方法[1,8]将表示大小与特定的符号或解码器配置挂钩,因此大得多或更复杂的场景可能需要再培训一个更高的容量模型. 后热压缩方法[7]减少一个已经重建的高斯集,但引入额外的每层处理或优化. 实际上,部署条件可能需要同样的模式,才能在不同的代表预算下运作。 简单地将一个预算不足的Top-K规则应用到一个常规训练的像素对齐模型上是不理想的:它可能会把高斯人过度分配到显著或高度不规则的地区,使得纹理薄弱的地区被覆盖。 因此,我们认为预算控制的高斯人紧凑是一个重要估计、空间覆盖和交叉视野冗余的共同问题,而不是简单的候选人排名。 这些局限性激励了一种向导模型,其最终的高斯代表可以在测试时进行调整,同时保留像素对齐重建的几何优势.

blocks.en: To this end, we propose BudgetSplat, a budget-controllable feed-forward 3D-GS framework that treats compact Gaussian allocation as a joint problem of importance estimation, spatial coverage, and cross-view redundancy. A single trained model supports varying context-view counts and user-specified test-time budgets without retraining or per-scene compression. Intra-Cross Mask Supervision provides structure-, coverage-, and redundancy-aware guidance for learning Gaussian importance, while Budget-Conditioned Feature Modulation adapts Gaussian prediction to the requested preservation ratio. Finally, Coverage-Aware Budget Selection combines local pre-selection, view-wise opacity ranking, and 3D redundancy suppression to construct the compact representation.
blocks.zh: 为此,我们提出预算平台(PresidentSplat),这是一个预算可控的向导3D-GS框架,将紧凑的高斯分配作为一个重要估计、空间覆盖和交叉视图冗余的共同问题。 一个经过培训的单一模式支持不同的上下文计数和用户指定的测试时间预算,而无需再培训或每场压缩。 Cross Mask 内部监督为学习高斯重要性提供结构,覆盖,和冗余意识指导,而预算-有条件的特性模块则根据要求的保存比例调整高斯预测. 最后,Profession-Award预算选择将本地预选,视网膜不透明排名和3D冗余压制结合起来,构建紧凑的表示.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • We formulate budget-controllable feed-forward 3D-GS as a joint problem of importance estimation, spatial coverage, and cross-view redundancy, and propose a single pixel-aligned model that supports different context-view counts and user-specified test-time budgets without retraining or per-scene compression. • We introduce Intra-Cross Mask Supervision to preserve informative structures, maintain sparse support in low-frequency regions, and reduce repeated cross-view supervision, together with Budget-Conditioned Feature Modulation that adapts Gaussian opacity and attributes to the requested preservation ratio. • We introduce Coverage-Aware Budget Selection, which combines patch-wise pre-selection, view-wise global opacity ranking, and 3D redundancy suppression to produce compact yet spatially distributed Gaussian representations. Experiments on ScanNet and Replica demonstrate robust quality–size trade-offs across different input-view settings and test-time budgets.

blocks.en: 2. Related Work
blocks.zh: 2. 相关工作

blocks.en: Generalizable novel view synthesis. NeRF [ 14 ] and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3D-GS) [ 9 ] achieve high-quality novel view synthesis but typically require per-scene optimization. Generalizable methods instead learn scene priors for feed-forward reconstruction. Early approaches predict image-conditioned radiance fields using pixel-aligned features, feature matching, or cost volumes [ 17 , 24 , 3 , 4 , 12 ] . Recent methods extend this paradigm to 3D-GS by directly predicting Gaussian geometry and attributes from input images [ 2 , 5 ] . DepthSplat [ 23 ] and MonoSplat [ 13 ] further incorporate pretrained monocular depth priors to improve geometry and generalization, but introduce additional dependence on external foundation models and feature adaptation. More importantly, these methods primarily target reconstruction quality and do not explicitly control the size of the final Gaussian representation.

blocks.en: Compact Gaussian representations. Pixel-aligned prediction provides strong geometric anchoring, but its Gaussian count scales with image resolution and input-view number, causing substantial cross-view redundancy. Geometry-aware fusion [ 20 , 21 ] and view compression [ 18 ] reduce repeated information, whereas voxel-aligned prediction [ 19 ] and scene-level decoders [ 1 , 8 ] redesign the prediction space to produce more compact representations. However, their output size is determined by the underlying fusion or representation design rather than a user-specified test-time budget. Post-hoc methods such as LightGaussian [ 7 ] compress an already reconstructed Gaussian set but require additional per-scene processing. EcoSplat [ 15 ] learns Gaussian importance and selects primitives through opacity ranking, but the final selection does not explicitly reason about spatial coverage or cross-view redundancy. In contrast, BudgetSplat treats controllable compaction as a joint importance–coverage–redundancy problem, introducing explicit low-frequency support, cross-view redundancy weighting, coverage-aware selection, and target-view alpha completion.

blocks.en: 3.1 Pixel-aligned Gaussian Estimation
blocks.zh: 3.1 与像素一致的高斯估计

blocks.en: We adopt FreeSplat’s feature extraction, cost-volume depth estimation, and Gaussian prediction backbone [ 20 ] , while removing its native geometric fusion module. Given posed context images, the backbone extracts multi-scale features, constructs a multi-view cost volume, and estimates per-pixel depth. The depth is unprojected to obtain Gaussian centers 𝝁 i ​ ( 𝒑 ) \bm{\mu}_{i}(\bm{p}) and corresponding base features 𝒇 i ​ ( 𝒑 ) \bm{f}_{i}(\bm{p}) . As described in the next section, the requested budget is subsequently injected into this feature before the Gaussian parameters are predicted. The resulting candidates are then processed by our coverage-aware budget selection strategy to construct the final representation. We retain the architecture of the FreeSplat-based prediction backbone without modification, while optimizing it jointly with the proposed budget-controlled components.

Coverage-Aware Budget Selection (CABS). Directly ranking all candidates within a view may concentrate the retained Gaussians in salient regions and leave smooth or weakly textured areas under-covered. We therefore perform coverage-aware selection in three steps.
First, each input view is divided into local patches, from which an oversampled set of high-opacity candidates is retained to construct a spatially distributed candidate pool.
Second, all candidates retained from the patches of the same view are ranked jointly according to their predicted opacity.
We refer to this step as view-wise global opacity ranking , since the ranking is performed across the candidate pool of one view rather than independently within each patch.
Finally, the ranked candidate pools from all views are jointly filtered by 3D non-maximum suppression to remove geometrically redundant candidates according to the requested budget.
The retained candidates form the compact Gaussian representation 𝒢 ρ \mathcal{G}_{\rho} . Detailed budget allocation and selection procedures are provided in the supplementary material.

blocks.en: Results on ScanNet. We evaluate our method on ScanNet [ 6 ] using 2, 3, and 10 context views. All settings use the same trained model, which also supports arbitrary preservation ratios at test time without retraining. Note that BudgetSplat 100% contains more Gaussians than native FreeSplat [ 20 ] because our model operates on the dense pixel-aligned candidate set and does not use its native geometric fusion. The lower-budget variants therefore reflect compaction by our selector rather than additional pruning of FreeSplat’s already fused output.

blocks.en: Zero-shot generalization on Replica. We further evaluate cross-dataset generalization by applying the models to Replica [ 16 ] without finetuning. As shown in Table 3 , we distinguish methods evaluated at their native output capacities from methods that explicitly perform budgeted Gaussian compaction. Among the budgeted-compaction methods, BudgetSplat achieves the strongest rendering quality. The results also show that absolute cross-dataset performance remains strongly influenced by the underlying reconstruction architecture and scene representation, as evidenced by the strong performance of VolSplat [ 19 ] and GlobalSplat [ 8 ] in different settings.

blocks.en: More importantly, BudgetSplat maintains stable rendering quality when the budget is reduced from 100 % 100\% to 25 % 25\% . blocks.en:
Our baseline applies plain view-wise opacity Top-K to retain 25% of the dense pixel-aligned Gaussians, without importance supervision or coverage-aware selection, resulting in severe performance degradation.
Adding intra-frame structure-and-coverage supervision in No.1 substantially improves all rendering metrics, showing that the pseudo masks provide an effective signal for learning Gaussian importance.
No.2 further introduces alpha completion, which improves all metrics. This indicates that local mask supervision alone does not guarantee complete target-view coverage, particularly under aggressive compression.
No.3 adds cross-frame redundancy weighting to No.2. The resulting improvement shows that reducing the supervision assigned to repeated observations encourages a less redundant allocation of Gaussians across views.
No.4 adds coverage-aware budget selection to No.2. Its larger improvement demonstrates that spatially distributed candidate selection helps prevent the retained Gaussians from collapsing into highly textured regions.
The full model achieves the best overall performance, confirming that the training-time importance guidance and inference-time selection strategy are complementary.
blocks.zh:
我们的基线采用纯视不透明 Top-K 来保留25%的稠密像素相通的高斯人,没有重要的监管或覆盖感知选择,导致性能严重退化.
在第1号中增加框架内结构与覆盖监督,大大改进了所有渲染度量,表明假面具为学习高斯的重要性提供了有效的信号.
第2号进一步引入了α补全,它改善了所有度量. 这表明,仅靠地方遮罩监督并不能保证完全覆盖目标视图,特别是在积极的压缩下.
第3号为第2号增加了跨框架冗余权重。 由此带来的改进表明,减少对反复观察的监督,有助于减少不同观点对高斯人的重复分配。
第4号在第2号中增加了了解覆盖面的预算选择。 其更大的改进表明,按空间分布挑选候选人有助于防止保留下来的高斯人崩溃为高度纹理化的地区。
全面模式取得了最佳的总体业绩,确认培训时间重要性指导和推断时间选择战略是相辅相成的。

blocks.en: 5. Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5.五. 结论

blocks.en:
We present BudgetSplat, a budget-controllable feed-forward 3D-GS. Instead of keeping all pixel-aligned Gaussians, BudgetSplat learns to compact them according to a user-specified budget ratio.
BudgetSplat can flexibly adjust the number of Gaussians while preserving rendering quality, without per-budget retraining or a separate offline compression stage. Experiments show that BudgetSplat provides an effective trade-off between visual quality, representation storage, rendering memory, and rendering efficiency.
blocks.zh:
我们提出预算板,一个预算可控的 3D -GS前卫。 PresidentSplact 而不是保留所有像素相通的高斯人,而是学会按照用户指定的预算比率进行压缩.
PresidentSplat可以在保留渲染质量的同时灵活调整高斯人的数量,而无需按预算进行再培训或单独进行离线压缩阶段. 实验显示,PresidentSplat在视觉质量,表现存储,渲染内存,渲染效率之间提供了有效的权衡.

blocks.en: Limitations and discussions. BudgetSplat relies on image gradients and estimated geometry for pseudo supervision, so degraded image quality or depth errors may affect selection under very compact budgets. Moreover, while BudgetSplat reduces the final representation and rendering costs, it retains the dense pixel-aligned prediction backbone. Future work will explore more robust supervision and budget-aware candidate generation.
blocks.zh: 限制和讨论。 PresidentSplat依赖于图像梯度和估计几何来进行伪监督,因此退化的图像质量或深度错误可能会影响非常紧凑的预算下的选择. 此外,虽然PresidentSplact降低了最终的表示和渲染成本,但它保留了密集的像素对齐的预测主干线. 今后的工作将探索更强有力的监督和具有预算意识的创造候选人。
